Ashok Roy Chaudhary vs State Of Gujarat & 3 on 6 October,
2015

Author: J.B.Pardiwala
Bench: J.B.Pardiwala
 R/Scr.A/5716/2015 O
 In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad
 Special Criminal Application (Quashing) No. 5716 of 2015
 ==========================================================
 Ashok Roy CHAUDHARY....Applicant(s)
 Versus
 State Of Gujarat & 3....Respondent(s)
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:

entities.text: High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr. Percy Kavina, Sr. Counsel with Mr Bhash H Mankad, Ms. Garima
 Malhotra And Ms. Neha Gupta, Advocates for the Applicant(s) No. 1
 Public Prosecutor for the Respondent(s) No. 1

The principal argument of Mr. Kavina, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the applicant - accused is that the applicant at no point of time was a Director in the company alleged to have committed the offence under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It is stated at para 2 of the petition that the applicant is under detention at Tihar Jail, Delhi since March 4, 2014 in the Contempt Petition (Civil) No. 412 of 2012.

He invited my attention to Section 66 of the Act,
2006, which creates a vicarious liability of the person who, at the time of the offence, is said to be in charge of, and responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company.

Mr. Kavina read over the entire complaint and prima-facie it appears that there is not a single averment in the complaint lodged by the Food Safety Officer of the Junagadh Municipal Corporation, that the applicant herein is the Director of the company and is responsible for the day-to-day affairs and management of the same.

The learned senior counsel has placed reliance on the following decisions of the Supreme Court:-
1. Harshendrakumar Vs. Rebatila Koley, reported in (2011) 3 SCC 351;
2. Gunmala Sales Pvt.Ltd. Vs. Anu Mehta, reported in (2015) 1 SCC 103.
Let notice be issued to the respondents, returnable on 6.1.2016.
